title: Microhoneycomb Monoliths Prepared by the Unidirectional Freeze-drying of Cellulose Nanofiber Based Sols: Method and Extensions
protocol: Suspend 66.7 g of Nadelholz Bleached Kraft Pulp in 700 mL of deionized water with a mechanical agitator at 300 rpm for 20 min.
Add 20 mL of aqueous TEMPO solution containing 0.15 g of TEMPO slowly to the NBKP suspension.
Add 20 mL of aqueous NaBr solution containing 1.5 g of NaBr slowly to the NBKP suspension.
Adjust the pH of the suspension to approximately 10.5 with 3.0 M NaOH solution.
Slowly add approximately 63.8 g of aqueous NaClO solution with a pipette to start TEMPO-mediated oxidation.
Continue adding 3.0 M NaOH solution during NaClO addition to maintain pH between 10.0 and ~10.5.
Rinse the oxidized cellulose fibers with deionized water three times, using 1,200 mL of DI water each time.
Treat the paste with a powerful mechanical blender to disintegrate oxidized cellulose fibers into nanofibers.
Add an equal amount of water during each mechanical treatment.
Obtain a 1 wt% TEMPO-mediated oxidized cellulose nanofiber (TOCN) sol.
Store the 1 wt% TOCN sol at 4 °C.
Add 0.21 g of SBR colloid into 10 g of 1 wt% TOCN sol in a 20 mL glass vessel.
Agitate the mixture with a vortex mixer for 3 min at power level 6.
Store the TOCN-SBR mixed sol at 4 °C before use.
Add 0.1 g of TiO2 nanoparticles into 10 g of 1 wt% TOCN sol in a 20 mL glass vessel.
Agitate the mixture with a homogenizer for 10 min to achieve an evenly mixed sol.
Store the TOCN-TiO2 mixed sol at 4 °C before use.
Reflux 1.7 g of carbon fiber in 150 mL of concentrated nitric acid at 60 °C for 6 h.
Add 0.01 g of treated carbon fiber into 10 g of 1 wt% TOCN sol inside a 20 mL glass vessel.
Shake-mix the mixture thoroughly.
Ultra-sonicate the mixture for 5 min to achieve an evenly mixed sol.
Store the mixture sol at 4 °C before use.
Load a polypropylene (PP) tube with glass beads and fill the bottom 5 cm part of the tube.
Load a certain amount of the 1 wt% TOCN sol into the PP tube containing glass beads.
Carefully remove any bubbles generated during the sol loading.
Keep the PP tube containing the TOCN sol at 4 °C overnight before use.
Attach the PP tube containing the TOCN sol to the dipping machine.
Set the relevant parameters for the dipping machine.
Start dipping the PP tube into a thermo jug containing liquid nitrogen at -196 °C at a constant speed of 50 cm/h.
Cut the PP tube part with a saw after dipping is complete.
Crack the frozen TOCN sol part into several sections using a saw or similar tool.
Freeze dry these sections with a freeze-drying machine at -10 °C for 1 day.
Continue freeze drying at -5 °C for 1 day.
Complete the freeze drying process at 0 °C for 1 day.
Load PP tubes with glass beads, filling the bottom 5 cm part of the tubes.
Load TOCN-SBR mixed sol or TOCN-TiO2 mixed sol into the PP tubes containing glass beads.
Load glass beads into the bottom 5 cm part of a PP tube (inner diameter: 13 mm, outer diameter: 15 mm, length: 150 mm).
Load an amount larger than 2.7 ml of TOCN-SOCF mixed sol into the PP tube containing glass beads.
Carefully remove bubbles generated during sol loading.
Keep the PP tube containing mixed sol at 4°C overnight before use.
Attach the PP tube containing the mixed solution to the dipping machine.
Set the relevant parameters and start dipping the PP tube into liquid nitrogen at a constant speed of 20 cm/h.
Cut the PP tube part with a saw.
Crack the frozen TOCN-SOCF solution part into several sections.
Freeze dry these sections with a freeze-drying machine at -10 °C for 1 day.
Continue freeze drying at -5 °C for 1 day.
Finally, freeze dry at 0 °C for 1 day.
Obtain the MHM-TOCN/SOCF as a white-grey monolith.
